in_sanskrit.name: अक्षर
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The imperishable, indivisible, and eternal, which is the symbol of the self and the Brahman.

in_hindi.name: अक्षर
in_hindi.long_meaning: It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'akshar' meaning letter, alphabet, syllable, phoneme. In Hinduism, Akshara is also considered as the symbol of the self and the Brahman, which is imperishable, indivisible, and eternal.

in_marathi.name: Akshara
in_marathi.long_meaning: Akshara हे एक हिंदू नाव आहे जे भारतीय संस्कृतीत खोल आध्यात्मिक महत्त्व ठेवते। The divine syllable, the beginning of the Vedas, the primordial sound from which the entire universe was created.

vedic_reference.note: Akshara is a significant term in Hinduism and Vedic literature. In the Vedas, Akshara is mentioned as the unmanifested form of the universe and the self. In the Hindu scripture, Bhagavad Gita, Krishna says that He is the Akshara Purusha, the immortal, imperishable, and eternal being.
